# Portable native Borland build

Run OdinBCC.exe on Windows. The GUI, Odin raw protocol engine and pinned LZ4 sources are compiled directly with classic BCC32 6.90 into one native x86 executable. No private Odin DLL or compiler RTL package is required. Keep LICENSE and NOTICE with the executable. Standard Windows libraries, including the system RichEdit control, and the selected phone driver are still required.

TCP/IP flashing: select TCP listen, leave `0.0.0.0:13579` or specify this PC's bind IPv4 address, start the operation, then connect a device supporting network Download mode to the PC. Allow incoming TCP in Windows Firewall if needed. TCP connect instead targets an already-listening device or relay. Each operation closes its connection; reconnect before another operation. Ordinary Android Wi-Fi/ADB is insufficient. Use a trusted network. TCP repartition supports selected-slot updates or a complete clean BL/AP/CP/CSC set, with mandatory PIT read-back verification. Physical TCP flashing and repartition remain unverified. See docs/TCP_FLASHING.md in the source repository.

This build synchronizes the stock-driver framing, slot selection, supported-device filtering, concise coloured logging and finalized-flash/reboot-warning fixes from EasyJTAG. LZ4 eligibility is audited before connection; eligible images use compressed transfer when negotiated, while unsupported profiles or devices without that capability use host-decoded raw transfer. It does not automatically retry a failed transfer. Protocols 4/5 require manufacturer-authenticated package metadata and DEVINFO policy. WinUSB remains at reviewed protocols 1–3. No phone operation starts automatically.

On a freshly opened exclusive Samsung serial handle, before I/O, startup requests the receive event mask, 4096-byte queue recommendations and a queue purge, then waits 500 ms with cancellation and deadline checks. The DCB stays unchanged and timeouts remain bounded. These calls follow observed Odin startup behavior, but do not prove identical driver behavior.

The supplied original-Odin capture records compressed SUPER sequences and a PIT upload, but ends mid-transfer; the user separately reported a later Odin PASS. The capture does not establish the cause of the earlier SUPER failure, and this restored Borland build has not been physically tried on that phone.

Normal flashing maps selected images to the first matching filename in the phone's live PIT order and uses that entry's identifier and type. Duplicate A/B filenames do not imply active-slot selection or automatically write both slots. A validated package PIT remains required for offline preflight, which uses package PIT order and may select a different row; complete package and live PITs need not match. The literal PIT filename `-` is a placeholder. eMMC type 2 uses 512-byte units and UFS type 8 uses 4096-byte units per partition; positive live block counts bound expanded image sizes. A zero count leaves capacity unknown: a normal write can proceed without inventing a size and may be rejected after writing begins. ABI 1.12 supports mixed units without a model/build/hash allowlist.

Explicit Re-partition / write PIT supports selected-slot updates or a complete clean BL/AP/CP/CSC set, using Samsung stock-driver or TCP transport; an optional separate raw PIT overrides the embedded firmware PIT. Select the archive containing the intended PIT or the raw target explicitly: repartitioning does not discover or substitute a PIT reference. The confirmation lists the explicitly selected archives or raw target. Preserve-data policy is not available. It selects the first matching target PIT row when A/B entries share a filename, without detecting the active slot or selecting both. It retains strict target-route and known-capacity checks, and verifies PIT read-back before image writes. Selected-slot updates exclude USERDATA, MISC and OMR images, but rewriting the PIT can alter or erase data. Ordinary flashing and the PIT reference archive never upload a PIT on their own. Physical repartition remains untested; see docs/REPARTITION.md in the source repository.

Archive verification supports older Samsung TAR.MD5 files with build-information text between the TAR and digest. The digest must verify over the exact TAR and build-information bytes, and the declared TAR size must identify a complete aligned TAR.

Native Debug/Release tests and owned-window offline firmware-plan checks pass. This native Borland build has not been physically flashed; the user-reported successful EasyJTAG flash is separate evidence.

Rebuild from the source project with build.ps1 or OdinBCC.cbproj. build-manifest.json records the shipped executable, compiler, source/header/object hashes, notices and Windows imports.

The 2026-10-18 application sync adds timestamped UTF-8 session logs, flushed directly by workers before GUI messages. Completion/join markers are file-only, and GUI processing does not duplicate saved messages. The engine remains statically linked; EasyJTAG's MinGW DLL-unload correction needs no equivalent DLL pin in this executable. Close the app before replacing the portable EXE.
